chapters.title: THE CABBAGE: EIGHTY-SEVEN REMEDIES. RECIPES MENTIONED BY CATO
chapters.finalPrompt:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: full-resolution chapter illustration for a deluxe digital edition of Pliny's Naturalis Historia, Book XX, chapter 9
Primary request: Create one independent, chapter-specific illustration of cabbage and the remedies attributed to Cato. In a broad Roman kitchen garden, show three complete living cabbage forms together in one continuous bed: a vigorous curly selinoides cabbage with parsley-like ruffled leaves, a broad-leaved helia or caulodes with leaves spreading from a thick stalk, and a compact bitter crambe with thin simple tightly packed leaves. Every outer leaf and each visible root crown must remain contained. In front of the bed, place one small freestanding circular stone preparation table, seen completely from rim to pedestal with air around it. On that table arrange a freshly cut raw cabbage heart in a mortar with an unmarked cup of oxymel, coriander seed, sprigs of rue and mint, a silphium root, a pinch of salt, and barley meal, faithfully evoking Cato's morning recipe. A small black-wine cup and one plain lidded pot for the twice-boiled preparation stand completely visible beside the table. Everything belongs to one coherent garden-and-kitchen scene, not a diagram, collage, atlas, contact sheet, or multiple framed panels.
Scene/backdrop: an orderly Roman hortus enclosed by a low wall, viewed from a low garden path at early morning; distant vine kept well apart from the cabbage bed; no dominant architecture or inscriptions

chapters.title: PETROSELINON; ONE REMEDY. BUSELINON; ONE REMEDY
chapters.finalPrompt:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: full-resolution chapter illustration for a deluxe digital edition of Pliny's Naturalis Historia, Book XX, chapter 12
Primary request: Create one independent, chapter-specific illustration of petroselinon and buselinon. In a rugged limestone cleft above a small mountain spring, show one complete petroselinon plant growing naturally from a rock fissure, with its root base, slender stalks, parsley-like leaves, flowers and seed all visibly contained. Below it, display one complete freshly lifted buselinon specimen on a flat stone: it must clearly differ through a notably shorter stalk and a distinct madder-red root, with all leaves and fine rootlets intact. Beside the plants, show their single measured preparation as one coherent mixing moment without hands: two small bronze spoons holding fresh petroselinon juice, one small unmarked cup of dark horehound juice with a horehound sprig beside it, and three matching small cups of steaming warm water arranged around one shallow mixing bowl. A single small non-threatening serpent may be shown fully visible while receding between distant stones, subordinate to the plants, recalling the chapter's remedy for serpent stings. Everything is one continuous rocky gathering scene, not a diagram, collage, atlas, contact sheet, or multiple framed panels.
